rows.scope: Vehicle Standard (Australian Design Rule 65/00 - Maximum Road Speed Limiting for Heavy Goods Vehicles and Heavy Omnibuses) 2006 (F2006L02297, clause 65.5.2 and applicability table, commenced 22 July 2006, continued under the Road Vehicle Standards Act 2018): 100 km/h maximum road speed capability for covered heavy goods vehicles (NC/N3) and heavy omnibuses (ME/M3 >5 t GVM), manufactured on or after 1 January 1991 for NC over 300 hp and ME over 14.5 t GVM, or 1 July 1991 for the remaining covered groups (NC up to 300 hp and ME over 5 t up to 14.5 t GVM; road trains follow state/territory authority under clause 65.5.1). Model proxy: applied as a country-wide cap for medium and heavy vehicles.

Royal Decree of 1 December 1975 (Highway Code Art. 11.2.1 a-b, >3.5 t MAM threshold in force 1 February 2007 under AR 21 December 2006 art. 1; belted 100 km/h-limited coach exception on motorways in force 1 April 2018): 90 km/h on motorways and physically separated roads with at least two lanes each way for vehicles and combinations over 3.5 t MAM and buses. Model proxy: applied as a country-wide cap for medium and heavy vehicles.

Brazilian Traffic Code (Lei 9.503/1997, Art. 61 para. 1 II a.2 and b.2, amended by Lei 13.281/2016 published 5 May 2016, in force 1 November 2016): 90 km/h default limit on dual- and single-carriageway paved rural highways ('rodovias') for other vehicles ('demais veiculos', including trucks and buses). Model proxy: applied as a country-wide cap for medium and heavy vehicles.

Regulation on the Implementation of the Road Traffic Safety Law of the PRC (State Council Decree No. 405, Art. 78 and Art. 115, in force 1 May 2004; unchanged in 2017 revision): 100 km/h expressway maximum for motor vehicles other than small passenger cars and motorcycles (covering trucks and buses). Model proxy: applied as a country-wide cap for medium and heavy vehicles.

Real Decreto 1428/2003 (Reglamento General de Circulacion, Art. 48.1.a, in force 23 January 2004; conventional-road limits amended by RD 1514/2018 without changing the motorway cap): 90 km/h on autopistas and autovias (80 km/h on conventional roads) for trucks, tractor units, vans and articulated vehicles; buses 100 km/h on motorways (in 2024 the 80 km/h exception for standing passengers or unbelted buses applied to conventional roads, extending to all roads outside towns only from 1 October 2026). Model proxy: applied as a country-wide cap for medium and heavy vehicles.

Code de la route Art. R413-8 (version amended by Decret n 2014-3 of 3 January 2014 art. 1, in force 10 January 2014): 90 km/h on motorways for vehicles over 3.5 t PTAC and combinations over 3.5 t PTRA, excluding public transport vehicles (also 90 km/h for vehicles up to 12 t on signed priority dual carriageways with a central reservation; 80 km/h on other rural roads; 60 km/h for >12 t combinations on non-priority roads). Model proxy: applied as a country-wide cap for medium and heavy vehicles.

Road Vehicles (Construction and Use) Regulations 1986 Reg. 36B(1A), (1B), (2) and (9) (as amended by S.I. 2004/2102, commenced 1 January 2005): 90 km/h stabilised speed-limiter setting for goods vehicles—under Reg. 36B(1A), those over 3,500 kg and not exceeding 12,000 kg maximum gross weight, first used on or after 1 January 2005, with a relevant attainable speed exceeding 90 km/h (alongside Euro III goods vehicles 3,500-12,000 kg from 1 October 2001 under Reg. 36B(1B) and vehicles over 12,000 kg from 1 January 1988 under Reg. 36B(2); certain domestic vehicles up to 7.5 t had transitional compliance until 1 January 2008; buses are separately governed by Reg. 36A). Model proxy: applied as a country-wide cap for medium and heavy vehicles.

Road Traffic (Ordinary Speed Limits - Buses, Heavy Goods Vehicles, Etc.) (Amendment) Regulations 2012 (S.I. No. 75/2012, Reg. 2 and Reg. 4(a), in operation 1 April 2012): 90 km/h ordinary motorway limit (80 km/h on other public roads) for Category N2 and N3 goods vehicles and combinations drawing Category O3 or O4 trailers. Model proxy: applied as a country-wide cap for medium and heavy vehicles.

Cabinet Order No. 43 of 2024 amending the Road Traffic Act Enforcement Order (NPA notification of 1 March 2024, in force 1 April 2024): 90 km/h statutory maximum on national expressway main carriageways for non-towing large and specified medium goods vehicles (defined by GVM, payload and seating thresholds under the Road Traffic Act; trailers remain 80 km/h; before 1 April 2024 the global 80 km/h fallback applies). Model proxy: applied as a country-wide cap for medium and heavy vehicles.

Land Transport (Road User) Rule 2004 (SR 2004/427, clauses 1.2 and 5.5(1), in force 27 February 2005): 90 km/h ordinary maximum speed limit on any road for heavy motor vehicles (GVM exceeding 3,500 kg; 45 km/h for certain unsprung vehicles under clause 5.5 and 80 km/h for school buses under clause 5.6). Model proxy: applied as a country-wide cap for medium and heavy vehicles.
